item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: What happens if an enclosed space with fishes is brought OUT of the red zone? Also, I'll assume license on behalf of "we don't understand why", but implosions due to perfect vacuums would be very weak. It's only a 1 atmosphere pressure difference, and you can't actually achieve a negative pressure. If there's something else going on to create a stronger vortex effect, that's fine, but at least one of the scientists should know his physics well enough to postulate that. ("immediately extradimensionally evacuated with sufficient force" doesn't really make sense, exactly… to be dangerous it would have to be actually exerting significant forces directly onto objects outside the enclosed space, or you just end up with violence to the enclosed and nothing more than a sudden vacuum to the rest)
